finding.claim: The /rss route passes the user-supplied query parameter `u` straight to open-uri's URI.open. The attacker picks the scheme and host and can reach internal services or cloud metadata (169.254.169.254). open-uri follows redirects, and the first 400 bytes of the response are returned to the caller, so this is full-read SSRF. Severity HIGH.
finding.source: params[:u] (HTTP GET query parameter `u` on /rss, app.rb:8)

trace.note: params[:u] is passed directly to URI.open with no parsing or validation
The first 400 bytes of the fetched body are returned in the response

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, scheme check, or host check on the path. The TRUSTED list at app.rb:5 is not used by this route. open-uri follows redirects (http/https/ftp), so there is no redirect restriction. No authentication middleware is present in the file.

verdict.reason: app.rb:8 passes the unauthenticated query param params[:u] straight to URI.open(...).read, and app.rb:9 returns the first 400 bytes. The TRUSTED check at app.rb:14 applies only to the separate /trusted route, and the file has no auth middleware or validation on /rss.
